scores.reasoning: The candidate demonstrates strong creative problem-solving with multiple concrete innovations and measurable outcomes, placing them in Tier 4 (7-8). Key evidence includes: (1) Guardian Assist - developed novel AI-powered clinical decision tool combining ambient AI with motivational interviewing for suicide risk detection, winning 1st place at VA MIT Grandhack and advancing to pilot phase; (2) Veterans Smart Call System - redesigned inpatient call light workflow, securing $5,000 funding; (3) COVID-19 PT protocols - created SOPs from scratch in unprecedented situation with no established protocols; (4) Dynamic scheduling system replacing inefficient paper/Excel systems. These are not just applications of existing methods but novel approaches with documented impact (awards, funding, pilot deployment). However, evidence falls short of Tier 5 (9-10) as innovations are within VA healthcare context rather than field-redefining contributions with wide external adoption.

evidence.quote: I pitched the idea for an ambient AI powered clinical decision tool that uses motivational interviewing prompts to guide clinicians during high-stakes conversations. I pitched the idea at the VA Hackathon in Tampa. Then built a wonderful team of SMEs around the idea and led the team through 3 phases of development in collaboration with Microsoft and VA stakeholders. We built Guardian Assist into a functional prototype at the conclusion of the VA Venture Studio Fellowship.
evidence.context: Demonstrates creative bridging of AI technology with clinical practice in novel way - combining ambient AI with motivational interviewing for suicide risk detection

scores.notes: Strong evidence of creativity with multiple concrete innovations. Pattern of innovation across multiple domains (AI tools, workflow systems, protocols). Score of 7 reflects consistent creative problem-solving with documented impact, but not yet at transformative/field-redefining level of 9-10.
